findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous when names or folder UIDs contain '_'.
findings.body:
The key joins `userUID`, `action`, `name` and `parent` with `_`. Dashboard and folder UIDs can contain `_`. So a dashboard named `a` in folder `b_c` and a dashboard named `a_b` in folder `c` both get the key `..._a_b_c`.

A denial cached for one resource then wrongly denies the other for the TTL. The early return in `Check` never looks at the real permissions.

Fix: use a separator that cannot appear in these values, or encode the parts (for example with a length prefix or `%q`).

findings.title: Cached denials hide newly granted permissions until the TTL runs out, defeating the DB requery.
findings.body:
Any `Check` that returns false now writes a denial entry for `shortCacheTTL`. Nothing clears that entry when permissions change. Later `Check` calls return at line 117 before the new 'requery the DB on a miss' path can run.

Trigger: a user asks for a resource before access exists, e.g. the frontend fetches a dashboard or folder during or right after creation, before the creator's permission is written, or an admin grants access or adds the user to a team after a denied request. That user then keeps getting `Allowed: false` for the whole TTL, even though the DB already allows it. This is the stale-permission problem the PR says it fixes, now for negative results.

Fix: give the denial cache a much shorter TTL, or clear or bypass it when permissions are written, so a fresh grant is seen at once.

findings.title: Denial-cache test caches `false` for dash1, so it passes even without the denial cache.
findings.body: The comment says this cache entry allows access so the test proves the denial cache wins. But the entry is `"dashboards:uid:dash1": false`, and the fake store returns no permissions. If the denial-cache lookup were removed, `Check` would still deny, so the test proves nothing. Set the entry to `true`.
